meta.title: Sandbox
meta.description: A hands-on sandbox for the Me2eM protocol: real seed phrases, derived Handles, stateless sessions — right in your browser.

hero.description: A hands-on demo of the protocol: generate a real seed phrase in your browser, watch Handles derive from it, and see one identity serve a person, a device, and an AI agent — with no personal data stored anywhere.

sandboxSeed.heading: Create your digital world
sandboxSeed.lead: Real cryptography, right in the browser: 12 words that exist nowhere else.
sandboxSeed.disclaimer: ⚠️ Demo: this phrase is real cryptography, but it is connected to nothing. It lives only on this page and vanishes when you leave. Do not use it as a real wallet.
sandboxSeed.copied: Copied to the clipboard. This is a convenience for testing. In real life you must write the seed down on paper. Press Hide — and the seed will be erased from this computer's memory, beyond recovery.
sandboxSeed.panelHidden: The seed is generated. This is the single most important secret of your world. Press Reveal to see it.
sandboxSeed.panelRevealed: The phrase is 128 bits of entropy packed into memorable words. The entire key hierarchy derives deterministically from it: Identity → Handle → SubHandle — the same seed yields the same keys on every device. Brute-forcing it is impossible: even a trillion guesses per second means billions of years.
sandboxSeed.paperPasteHint: Paste the seed from the clipboard here.
sandboxSeed.paperNote: Seed must be stored offline: paper — yes; screenshots, cloud notes, password managers — no. Electronic copies are attack surface. If these words leak, your identity leaks with them.
sandboxSeed.verifyPrompt: Enter words {a}, {b} and {c} of your seed phrase
sandboxSeed.verifyError: The words do not match your seed phrase. Check your notes.
sandboxSeed.verifySeeAgain: I need to see the seed phrase again
sandboxSeed.paperMissing: You haven't written the seed down. Go back and copy the seed onto your paper — a seed that isn't recorded cannot be kept.
sandboxSeed.paperBadgeHint: Click a word from your paper to fill the field.
sandboxSeed.bornText: The entire key hierarchy derives deterministically from these 12 words: Identity → Handle → SubHandle. Zero bytes on the server.
sandboxSeed.createdSequence: What just happened: you generated 128 bits of entropy in your browser — it derived your root Identity — you proved you hold the paper — your world exists. Nowhere along the way was a single byte stored on a server.

human.title: Multi-Context Identity
human.description: One root Identity → isolated Handles, created one at a time. Each context gets its own profile, keypair, and Solana wallet — no shared credentials.
human.noteFamily: ✓ Work handle ready. Deriving one handle reveals nothing about the others — the family context is a fresh keypair from the same seed.
human.noteGym: ✓ Family handle ready. One more derivation and you have a fully separate sports identity.
human.footerDone: All three contexts derived — same seed, same order of derivation paths, zero shared credentials between them.

labels.wallet: Solana Wallet — derived from the same seed

satellite.title: Satellite Tasking Marketplace
satellite.description: Identity = Mission Control · Handle = satellite · SubHandle = instrument. A buyer purchases a time-boxed tasking window on an instrument — the access document is an access certificate signed by Mission Control for the buyer's own key.
satellite.mccNote: Everything below is derived deterministically from YOUR seed: the same seed always rebuilds the same fleet, instruments, and wallets.

labels.subject: Subject (buyer)
labels.verifiedOffline: verified offline — MCC public key only

agent.title: AI Agent Mandate & Revocation
agent.description: Owner issues a time-boxed mandate (attestation) to an AI agent. The agent signs its own session. Revoking a session stops one request; revoking the attestation is the one-call kill switch — the agent is disabled across every service, future sessions included.
agent.placeholder: Run the scenario to demonstrate AI agent mandate and revocation.

steps.revokeSessionDetail: Session JTI added to in-memory revocation set
steps.sessionAfterFail: ✗ Expected revocation to fail, but it passed
steps.newSession: The agent simply makes a new session
steps.newSessionWarn: ⚠ New JTI verifies fine — revoking sessions one by one cannot stop a compromised agent
steps.killSwitchDetail: The mandate's JTI {jti} enters the same revocation store; verifiers check every JTI in the presented chain, not only the session id.
steps.futureAfterOk: ✓ MANDATE DEAD — the agent is disabled across every service it touches, including all future sessions
steps.futureAfterFail: ✗ Expected the mandate revocation to kill future sessions

sso.title: Multi-App SSO (UC-4)
sso.description: One seed phrase is the whole account system. The user types it once at the first app; every other app in the ecosystem logs them in through the instance cookie. Perimeter apps verify statelessly (Mode 1), an external partner goes through the attestation chain (Mode 2) — and "log out everywhere" is one revocation entry.
sso.ctaTaxi: 1 · Sign in — App A (taxi), seed typed once
sso.ctaFreelance: 2 · Open App B (freelance) — auto login, no re-entry
sso.simNote: Taxi sees {taxiHandle}, freelance sees {freelanceHandle} — different keys, so the two apps cannot correlate the same person. Correlation is the user's choice.
sso.cookieNote: The next app under the domain presents this cookie — the instance recognizes it and signs the user in. No password, no seed re-entry.
sso.partnerSubtitle: offline · root public key only · attestation JTI {jti}
sso.partnerReceivesValue: session token + attestation chain — no shared perimeter
sso.partnerResultOk: ✓ verified with the public key alone
sso.logoutTitle: Log out everywhere — {count} JTI entries, that was the whole logout.
sso.logoutDetail: Taxi rejects: {taxi} · Freelance rejects: {freelance} · Partner rejects: {partner} — no database wipe, just revocation entries every verifier consults.

ev.title: EV Charging Network (UC-2)
ev.description: Stations never need a network: the operator attests each station once at install, the station derives and attests its connectors locally, sessions are signed onboard — and an independent charging app authorizes them with the operator's public key alone. Compromising a station is contained by its grant.
ev.ctaCharge: 3 · Start a charging session (app verifies offline)
ev.grantNote: The grant is the blast radius: a broken-in station can only attest connector-* names, only charge:* scopes, only sessions under TTL 7200.
ev.revokeTitle: Station revoked — one JTI ({jti}) contained the whole station.
ev.revokeDetail: A brand-new connector session (valid signature, valid chain structure) is rejected: {result} — every verifier that checks JTIs stops trusting station-001 at once.

labels.verifiedOk: ✓ chain operator → station → connector, public key only · offline

commerce.title: Agent Commerce — Paid APIs (UC-7)
commerce.description: The buyer is a machine: an AI agent with its own key, its own mandate, and its own seed-derived wallet calls a paid API. The seller verifies the mandate offline, quotes via HTTP 402, the agent signs once, the facilitator settles. No accounts, no cards, no billing database.
commerce.ctaPaidCall: 2 · Call the paid API (402 → sign → settle)
commerce.agentTitle: Commerce Agent — own key, own mandate, own wallet
commerce.sellerTitle: Seller API — a real third party
commerce.agentNote: One 64-byte seed derives both the Identity and the Solana wallet — the agent pays from the same root its mandate grows from.
commerce.wireTitle: wire — what actually crossed the network
commerce.simNote: Transport is simulated in-page (the seller and facilitator run in your browser) — but the client is the real @me2em/x402 loop: every signature and mandate verification is real. On-chain settlement is simulated: devnet holds no funds.
commerce.receipt: Settlement tx {tx} · {amount} lamports · payer = mandate-bound agent wallet
commerce.negativeTitle: Mandate enforced — HTTP {status}, blocked before any payment.
commerce.negativeDetail2: No 402 was ever issued for this API: the seller rejected the session first. A mandate cannot be widened — not even to spend money.
commerce.hint: The agent's session will be signed with its own key — the owner's seed never enters the agent runtime.
